docs.title: ragpick
docs.text:
Choose, build, evaluate, and run the right RAG architecture.

Most RAG projects don't fail because of the LLM. They fail because the architecture was picked by guesswork: vector search where exact product codes matter, no access control for internal documents, no evidence that the "improved" pipeline is actually better.

ragpick turns that choice into an engineering process:

  1. Describe your requirements (corpus size, keyword-heavy queries, latency, access control) and ragpick recommend explains which blueprint fits and why.
  2. Define the pipeline as YAML. Architecture as code, validated with readable errors.
  3. Evaluate competing blueprints on your data with ragpick eval and pick the winner from numbers, not vibes.

ragpick sits next to LangChain and LlamaIndex rather than replacing them. It owns the interfaces, config, selector and evaluation; other libraries plug in as components.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install ragpick              # core, offline components
pip install "ragpick[openai]"    # + OpenAI embeddings and chat models
pip install "ragpick[all]"       # + sentence-transformers, Qdrant, PDF

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Concepts: components, blueprints, the selector, access control.
  • Blueprints: what each architecture is good at.
  • Config reference: every rag.yaml key.
  • Writing a plugin: add your own loader, store, or model.
  • Evaluation: metrics and how to compare configs.
  • Design decisions: the choices behind v0.1.

docs.title: LangChain and LlamaIndex adapters
docs.text:
ragpick works alongside LangChain and LlamaIndex rather than replacing them. Any of their loaders, embedding models, retrievers and LLMs can be used as a ragpick component, with ragpick's config, access control, selector and evaluation around it.

Neither framework is a ragpick dependency. The adapters only call public methods (embed_documents, invoke, get_text_embedding_batch, retrieve, …), so install the LangChain or LlamaIndex packages you want yourself:

pip install ragpick langchain-openai          # or: pip install ragpick llama-index
Kind type: langchain wraps type: llamaindex wraps loader a document loader (lazy_load() / load()) a reader (load_data()), default SimpleDirectoryReader embedder Embeddings (embed_documents, embed_query) an embedding model (get_text_embedding_batch, get_query_embedding) retriever a retriever (invoke(query)) a retriever (retrieve(query)) generator a chat model (invoke(messages)) an LLM (complete(prompt))

docs.title: From YAML
docs.text:
Give the class's import path and its constructor arguments:

blueprint: hybrid
components:
  loader:
    type: langchain
    params:
      class_path: langchain_community.document_loaders.PyPDFLoader
      path_arg: file_path               # the constructor argument that receives the path
  embedder:
    type: langchain
    params:
      class_path: langchain_openai.OpenAIEmbeddings
      kwargs: {model: text-embedding-3-small}
  generator:
    type: llamaindex
    params:
      class_path: llama_index.llms.openai.OpenAI
      kwargs: {model: gpt-4o-mini, temperature: 0}

class_path accepts package.module.Class or package.module:Class. A missing package fails with a clear "could not import … install the package" message.

Treat configs as code

class_path imports and instantiates arbitrary Python classes. Only load rag.yaml files you trust, just as you would only run code you trust.

docs.title: From Python
docs.text:
Pass objects you've already built:

from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI, OpenAIEmbeddings
from ragpick import Pipeline, load_config
from ragpick.adapters import LangChainEmbedder, LangChainGenerator

pipeline = Pipeline(
    load_config("rag.yaml"),
    components={
        "embedder": LangChainEmbedder(embeddings=OpenAIEmbeddings(model="text-embedding-3-small")),
        "generator": LangChainGenerator(chat_model=ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o-mini")),
    },
)

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
• Generators use ragpick's grounded prompt and citation parsing, and also work as an evaluation judge (eval.judge: {type: langchain, params: {...}}). LangChain token usage comes from usage_metadata; LlamaIndex usage is estimated.
  • Embedders use the framework's query-embedding method for searches and its document-embedding method for indexing.
  • Loaders turn source / file_path metadata into document ids relative to the ingested path. When one file yields several documents (PDF pages), :<n> is appended.
  • Retrievers are for indexes managed outside ragpick. External retrievers can't apply ragpick filters, so filters and allowed_groups access control are applied to their results afterwards (post-filtering). Configure the external retriever to return enough candidates for that. Missing scores become 1 / rank.

docs.title: Blueprints
docs.text:
Run ragpick blueprints to see this list in your terminal.

Blueprint Status Best for naive stable prototypes, small corpora, natural-language questions over prose hybrid stable the default for commercial systems; keyword-heavy domains; medium and large corpora parent_child stable long structured documents where answers need surrounding context sql planned structured data and analytics questions (text-to-SQL) graph planned multi-hop and "main themes" questions (GraphRAG) agentic planned complex questions needing several lookups or tools corrective planned noisy corpora: grade retrieval, rewrite, or fall back

docs.title: naive
docs.text:
directory loader → recursive chunker (800/100) → embedder → memory store
→ vector retriever → generator

The simplest architecture that works. Its weak spot is exact terms: an embedding of "E-4017" is barely different from "E-4071", so error codes, SKUs and legal references are often missed.

docs.title: hybrid
docs.text:
┌→ vector search ─┐
query (+ ACL filters) ─┤                 ├→ RRF fusion → [cross-encoder] → generator
                       └→ BM25 search ───┘

BM25 catches exact terms and vectors catch paraphrases. Reciprocal Rank Fusion combines the two rankings without score calibration:

score(chunk) = Σ_lists  weight / (rrf_k + rank)        (rrf_k = 60 by default)

Tune it in your config:

blueprint: hybrid
components:
  retriever:
    params: {k: 20, rrf_k: 60, candidates: 40, vector_weight: 1.0, keyword_weight: 1.0}
  reranker: {type: cross_encoder}          # pip install "ragpick[rerank]"

On the bundled example dataset (keyword-heavy support questions), hybrid beats naive on hit rate and MRR even with the offline fake embedder:

ragpick eval examples/eval.jsonl --config examples/naive.yaml --config examples/hybrid.yaml

docs.title: parent_child
docs.text:
document ─→ parent sections (2000 chars) ─→ child chunks (400 chars) ─→ indexed
query ─→ hybrid search over children ─→ dedupe by parent ─→ parent sections ─→ generator

Small chunks are precise to search but often too small to answer from; large chunks give context but match poorly. parent_child does both: it searches children and hands the LLM each matching child's whole parent section. Each child stores its parent's text in metadata (parent_id, parent_text), so it works with every store and needs no extra document store. Citations and contexts use parent ids (manual.md#3).

blueprint: parent_child
components:
  chunker:
    params: {parent_size: 2000, parent_overlap: 0, child_size: 400, child_overlap: 50}
  retriever:
    params: {k: 5, base: hybrid, child_k: 20}   # base: hybrid | vector
query:
  top_k: 3        # parents are big: fewer contexts keep prompts reasonable

Trade-offs: bigger prompts, and parent text is stored once per child. Set requirements.long_documents: true and ragpick recommend will suggest it.

docs.title: Adding a blueprint
docs.text:
A blueprint is one YAML file in src/ragpick/blueprints/:

metadata:
  name: my_blueprint
  description: One paragraph on what it does.
  best_for: [...]
  tradeoffs: [...]
  status: stable          # or planned
defaults:
  components: {...}       # same schema as rag.yaml `components`
  query: {top_k: 5}

Add a test that builds it (see tests/test_blueprints.py) and, if it should be recommended, a selector rule. See CONTRIBUTING.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
A pipeline is made of small, swappable components. Each one is a typing.Protocol in ragpick.interfaces, so any object with the right methods works. No base class is needed.

Kind Protocol Built-in types loader load(path) -> Iterable[Document] directory, text, pdf, langchain, llamaindex chunker split(docs) -> list[Chunk] recursive, fixed, parent_child embedder embed(texts), dimension (optional embed_query) fake, openai, sentence_transformers, langchain, llamaindex store add, search, delete, persist, load memory, qdrant keyword_index add, search, persist, load bm25 retriever retrieve(query, k, filters) vector, keyword, hybrid, parent_child, langchain, llamaindex reranker rerank(query, chunks, top_n) none, cross_encoder generator generate(query, contexts) -> Answer fake, openai, ollama, langchain, llamaindex

Data flows through these models: Document → Chunk → RetrievedChunk → Answer (text, citations as chunk ids, contexts, usage).

Ingest: loader → chunker → embedder → store (+ keyword index) → persisted to index_dir.

Query: retriever (with ACL filters) → reranker → generator → Answer.

docs.title: Blueprints
docs.text:
A blueprint is a named, tested architecture: a YAML file with metadata (description, best_for, tradeoffs, status) and default components. Your rag.yaml names a blueprint and overrides only what differs:

blueprint: hybrid
components:
  embedder:  {type: openai, params: {model: text-embedding-3-small}}
  generator: {type: openai, params: {model: gpt-4o-mini}}

See Blueprints for the catalogue and roadmap.

docs.title: Architecture as code
docs.text:
rag.yaml is validated by Pydantic. Mistakes are reported with their YAML key path:

Invalid configuration in rag.yaml:
  - query.topk: unknown key (check for typos)
  - components.retriever: required key is missing (set it, or choose a `blueprint` that provides it)

Layers merge as blueprint defaults → rag.yaml → --set flags. Secrets come from the environment with ${OPENAI_API_KEY} and are never written back to disk. Check the merged result with ragpick validate.

docs.title: The selector
docs.text:
ragpick recommend runs a table of explainable rules over your requirements:

Situation Effect long, structured documents parent_child small corpus, not keyword-heavy naive keyword-heavy, or medium/large corpus hybrid structured data (sql, csv, …) sql (planned) → warns and falls back to hybrid latency: low reranker disabled, with a reason access_control with a store that cannot filter warning large corpus on the in-memory store warning, suggests Qdrant pdf data without ragpick[pdf] warning

To settle it with data instead of rules, ragpick bench runs every stable blueprint on your documents and questions; see Evaluation.

Every recommendation lists reasons, alternatives and warnings. The rules live in ragpick.selector.rules.RULES and are easy to extend.

docs.title: Access control
docs.text:
Document-level access control is built in. Attach groups to a document with Markdown front matter (or any loader's metadata):

---
allowed_groups: [support]
---
# Internal escalation guide

Then query as a member of some groups:

p.query("How do I escalate?", groups=["support"])

ragpick query "How do I escalate?" --groups support

Rules:

  • Chunks without allowed_groups are public.
  • Chunks with it are returned only if the caller's groups intersect it.
  • groups=None (or no --groups) means public chunks only. This is secure by default.
  • Filtering happens inside every store and the BM25 index before ranking, so restricted text never reaches fusion, reranking, or the LLM.

Other metadata filters use the same mechanism: p.query(q, filters={"lang": ["en", "de"]}).

docs.title: Config reference
docs.text: Layers merge in this order: blueprint defaults → your rag.yaml → CLI --set. Within components, changing a component's type replaces it entirely; keeping the type merges params. Strings may use ${ENV_VAR} or ${ENV_VAR:-default}. Relative paths (data, index_dir) resolve against the config file's directory.

docs.title: Top level (rag.yaml)
docs.text:
Top-level schema of rag.yaml.

Key Type Default Description version 1 1 Config schema version. name str 'ragpick-app' Application name. blueprint str | null None Blueprint supplying default components. data str | null None Default source path for ragpick ingest / ragpick eval. requirements Requirements see section Inputs for ragpick recommend. components ComponentsConfig required Pipeline components (usually partly supplied by the blueprint). query QueryConfig see section Query-time settings. eval EvalConfig see section Evaluation settings. index_dir str '.ragpick/index' Where indexes are persisted.

docs.title: requirements
docs.text:
What the application needs. Used by the selector (ragpick recommend).

Key Type Default Description data_types list[str] ['markdown'] Kinds of source data, e.g. markdown, pdf, html, sql, csv. corpus_size small | medium | large 'small' small (<1k chunks), medium, or large (>100k chunks). keyword_heavy bool False Queries rely on exact terms: product codes, legal terms, IDs. long_documents bool False Documents are long and structured (manuals, policies, contracts). latency low | normal 'normal' low disables expensive stages. needs_citations bool True Answers must cite their sources. access_control bool False Documents are restricted to groups (allowed_groups metadata).

docs.title: components
docs.text:
The components that make up a pipeline.

Key Type Default Description loader ComponentSpec required Turns a path into documents. chunker ComponentSpec required Splits documents into chunks. embedder ComponentSpec required Embeds chunks and queries. store ComponentSpec required Vector store. keyword_index ComponentSpec | null None Keyword index (required by the hybrid and keyword retrievers). retriever ComponentSpec required Retrieval strategy. reranker ComponentSpec see section Optional reranker. generator ComponentSpec required Answer generator (LLM).

docs.title: Component spec (each entry of components, and eval.judge)
docs.text:
A component reference: registry type plus constructor params.

Key Type Default Description type str required Registered component name, e.g. openai or bm25. params dict[str, Any] {} Keyword arguments passed to the component.

docs.title: query
docs.text:
Query-time settings.

Key Type Default Description top_k int 5 Number of contexts passed to the generator.

docs.title: eval
docs.text:
Evaluation settings.

Key Type Default Description judge ComponentSpec | null None Generator used as LLM judge (must support complete). prices dict[str, PriceSpec] {} Model name → price; merged over ragpick's built-in price table.

docs.title: Price spec (each entry of eval.prices)
docs.text:
Price of a model in USD per one million tokens.

Key Type Default Description prompt_per_1m float 0.0 completion_per_1m float 0.0

docs.title: Design decisions
docs.text: Where the v0.1 brief left a choice open, ragpick picked the simplest option that keeps the interfaces extensible. Each decision is listed here so it can be revisited.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
1. Component type change replaces the component. When a layer (your YAML or a --set flag) changes a component's type, the blueprint's params for that component are dropped, because they belong to a different class (e.g. dimension for fake makes no sense for openai). If the type stays the same, params are merged key by key.
  2. CLI flags are generic --set key.path=value overrides, parsed as YAML scalars, instead of one flag per setting. A few common settings also have dedicated flags (query --top-k, query --groups).
  3. Relative paths resolve against the config file's directory, not the current directory, so ragpick eval --config examples/naive.yaml works from anywhere.
  4. New data key (optional) holds the default source path for ingest and is used by eval to build an index automatically when none exists.
  5. ${VAR} without a default fails loudly with the key path. ${VAR:-default} provides a fallback. Interpolation only happens in memory; ragpick init never writes secrets, and ragpick validate masks secret-looking keys (*key*, *token*, *secret*, *password*).
  6. components is required when no blueprint is set. There is no implicit default blueprint; the error message suggests setting one.

docs.title: Blueprints and components
docs.text:
1. Stable blueprints default to fake embedder and generator. A blueprint describes the architecture (chunking, retrieval, fusion, reranking); the model provider is a separate choice. This makes every blueprint runnable offline. ragpick init asks for a provider (fake, openai, ollama), and --yes defaults to fake. Using the fake generator is logged at INFO level.
  2. Planned blueprints are YAML files with metadata only. ragpick blueprints shows the roadmap from the same source of truth; loading one raises a clear error.
  3. Dependency injection by constructor parameter name. The pipeline passes embedder, store and keyword_index to any component whose constructor declares a parameter with that name. Plugins get the same treatment without registration hooks.
  4. A retriever that needs a keyword index gets bm25 automatically when components.keyword_index is not set.
  5. Re-ingest is an upsert per document: chunks of re-ingested documents are deleted first; other documents in the index are kept.
  6. Chunk ids are "<doc_id>#<n>"; doc ids are paths relative to the ingested directory. These ids are what relevant_doc_ids in eval datasets refer to.
  7. The index records its embedder in ragpick.json; querying with a different embedder config fails with a "re-ingest" message instead of returning garbage.
  8. Separate Registry instances start empty. Only the global registry loads built-ins, which keeps isolated tests simple. Registry.remove() exists for cleanup.
  9. Entry points are named "<kind>.<name>" and point at the factory. An entry point without a dot is just imported (side-effect registration). Broken plugins are logged and skipped.

docs.title: Access control and filters
docs.text:
1. Filters are a plain dict. A scalar value means equality, a list means in, list-valued metadata matches on intersection, and a chunk missing the key does not match.
  2. allowed_groups is special. Chunks without it are public, and chunks with it require a group intersection. allowed_groups: [] means "nobody".
  3. Secure by default. Pipeline.query(groups=None) returns public chunks only. ACL filtering happens inside the stores and BM25 before ranking, so restricted text never reaches fusion, reranking, or the LLM.
  4. Document metadata comes from Markdown front matter. That's how allowed_groups is attached to files. Programmatic loaders can set any metadata.
  5. Qdrant ACL: implemented as is_empty(allowed_groups) OR match_any(groups). Because Qdrant's is_empty also matches [], an empty list is stored as a private sentinel so "nobody" is not treated as "public".

docs.title: Generation
docs.text:
1. The model sees numeric citations [1]; Answer.citations holds chunk ids (stable, meaningful outside the prompt). Out-of-range numbers are ignored.
  2. No contexts → "I don't know." without calling the LLM.
  3. TextCompleter protocol (complete(system, user)) gives raw LLM access for judges; LLM generators implement both it and Generator. The fake generator's complete returns a fixed, configurable string (a constant-score fake judge for plumbing tests).
  4. Answer.usage.latency_ms covers the whole query (retrieval + generation).

docs.title: Evaluation
docs.text:
1. Retrieval metrics are computed over the ranked context list mapped to doc_ids. precision@k divides by k even when fewer than k contexts are returned. Rows without relevant_doc_ids are excluded from retrieval averages.
  2. k is the config's query.top_k.
  3. Eval rows may carry groups, so access-controlled questions can be evaluated.
  4. eval --data PATH ingests into a temporary index per config, so comparisons never overwrite real indexes. Without --data, the config's existing index is used, built from data if missing.
  5. Cost is estimated for generation tokens only, from a built-in price table that eval.prices can extend or override. Unknown models show n/a. Judge tokens are not included.
  6. Judge failures and query errors are recorded per row and counted in errors; they don't abort the run.

docs.title: v0.2
docs.text:
1. Parent text lives in child metadata (parent_id, parent_text) instead of a new "document store" interface. It costs storage, but works unchanged with every VectorStore, BM25 and persistence path, including Qdrant.
  2. parent_child retriever wraps a base retriever (hybrid default, or vector) and fetches child_k (default 4 * k) children to find k distinct parents. Parent contexts get the best child's score and keep the child's source.
  3. Selector: long_documents (priority 60) beats keyword_heavy (50), because parent_child already uses hybrid search for children. Structured data (100) still wins.
  4. ragpick bench uses one top_k for every blueprint (base config's, or 5), otherwise metrics are not comparable. The base config supplies providers; architecture keys (chunker, keyword_index, retriever, reranker) always come from each blueprint. Ties on the metric go to lower p50 latency. The written winner config is built from the uninterpolated base YAML, so ${ENV_VAR} secrets are never expanded into it.
  5. Adapters depend on nothing. They call public methods (embed_documents, invoke, get_text_embedding_batch, …) and build objects from class_path + kwargs, so ragpick doesn't pin LangChain/LlamaIndex versions. The inner constructor arguments are called kwargs to avoid confusion with the component's own params.
  6. External retrievers are post-filtered for metadata filters and allowed_groups, because they can't apply ragpick filters themselves.
  7. embed_query is an optional embedder method, used by retrievers for queries when present (asymmetric models), so the Embedder protocol stays unchanged.
  8. setup-uv is pinned to an exact version (v10.3.3) because it no longer publishes major tags, and sets activate-environment: true, which newer versions no longer imply.

docs.title: Tooling
docs.text:
1. types-PyYAML is not a dev dependency (it wasn't in the approved list), so mypy treats yaml as untyped via an override. Adding the stub package would be a one-line improvement.
  2. Interactive questions use rich.prompt (Prompt.ask(choices=...), Confirm.ask). Recent typer releases no longer depend on click and typer.prompt does not accept choice types; rich is already a core dependency, so this works on every supported typer version.

docs.title: Evaluation
docs.text: Choosing a blueprint should be backed by numbers from your data. ragpick eval runs one or more configs over a question set and prints a comparison table.

docs.title: Dataset format
docs.text:
JSON Lines, one question per line. Only question is required:

{"question": "What does error E-1042 mean?", "ground_truth": "Low battery.", "relevant_doc_ids": ["error-codes.md"]}
{"question": "When do we escalate to Tier 2?", "relevant_doc_ids": ["internal-escalation.md"], "groups": ["support"]}
Field Purpose question The query. relevant_doc_ids Document ids (paths relative to the ingested directory) that answer it. Enables retrieval metrics. ground_truth Reference answer, stored in the results for review. groups Run the query as a member of these groups (to evaluate access-controlled content). id Optional identifier.

Blank lines and lines starting with # or // are ignored. Errors name the file and line.

docs.title: Running
docs.text:
# compare two configs; each gets a temporary index built from --data
ragpick eval examples/eval.jsonl \
  --config examples/naive.yaml --config examples/hybrid.yaml \
  --data examples/data --output results.json

Without --data, each config uses its persisted index and builds it from the config's data path if none exists. --output writes .json (all rows) or .csv (one row per config).

From Python:

from ragpick import Pipeline
from ragpick.eval import evaluate, load_dataset

report = evaluate(Pipeline.from_yaml("rag.yaml"), load_dataset("eval.jsonl"))
print(report.metrics)

docs.title: Bench: try every blueprint
docs.text:
ragpick bench answers "which blueprint should I use?" with data. It runs every stable blueprint on your documents and questions, using the same models and the same top_k, and ranks them:

ragpick bench eval.jsonl --data ./docs --config rag.yaml --metric mrr --write best.yaml
  • Providers (loader, embedder, store, generator, eval settings) come from the base --config (default: ./rag.yaml if present, otherwise offline fake components).
  • Architecture (chunker, keyword index, retriever, reranker) comes from each blueprint.
  • --metric picks the winner: hit_rate@k, mrr (default), precision@k, or, with a judge, faithfulness / answer_relevance. Ties go to the lower median latency.
  • -b NAME (repeatable) limits the candidates; --top-k overrides k for all of them.
  • --write best.yaml saves the winner's config: your providers plus blueprint: <winner>. Secrets stay as ${ENV_VAR} references.
  • Each candidate gets a temporary index; your real indexes are never touched.
from ragpick.eval.bench import run_bench

result = run_bench("eval.jsonl", "./docs", base_config="rag.yaml", metric="mrr")
print(result.winner, result.ranking)

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
Retrieval (no LLM needed). These are computed over the ranked contexts mapped to their doc_id, with k = query.top_k:

Metric Definition hit_rate@k 1 if any of the top-k contexts comes from a relevant document. mrr 1 / rank of the first relevant context (0 if none). precision@k relevant contexts in the top k, divided by k.

LLM-judged. These need a judge (eval.judge in the config or --judge openai:gpt-4o-mini):

Metric Question asked of the judge faithfulness Is every claim in the answer supported by the retrieved contexts? answer_relevance Does the answer address the question directly?

Each score is 0–1 with a short reason per row (in the JSON output). All judge prompts live in ragpick/eval/prompts.py.

Operational:

Metric Definition latency_p50_ms / latency_p95_ms end-to-end query latency percentiles total_tokens prompt + completion tokens of the generator est_cost_usd from the price table (USD per 1M tokens); n/a for unknown models errors rows where the query or judge failed (recorded, not fatal)

Override or extend prices in the config:

eval:
  judge: {type: openai, params: {model: gpt-4o-mini}}
  prices:
    my-finetuned-model: {prompt_per_1m: 0.30, completion_per_1m: 1.20}

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• 30–100 representative questions catch most regressions. Include the exact-term queries your users really send (codes, IDs), plus some that should return "I don't know".
  • Add eval to CI: run ragpick eval ... --output results.json and fail the build if hit_rate@k drops.
  • The fake generator and judge are for plumbing tests. Their answer metrics aren't meaningful, but retrieval metrics are.

docs.title: Writing a plugin
docs.text: Any class that satisfies a protocol from ragpick.interfaces can be a component. Register it and refer to it by name in rag.yaml.

docs.title: 1. Implement the protocol
docs.text:
# ragpick_cohere/__init__.py
import cohere


class CohereEmbedder:
    """Cohere embeddings for ragpick."""

    def __init__(self, model: str = "embed-english-v3.0", api_key: str | None = None) -> None:
        self.model = model
        self._client = cohere.Client(api_key)

    @property
    def dimension(self) -> int:
        return 1024

    def embed(self, texts: list[str]) -> list[list[float]]:
        response = self._client.embed(texts=texts, model=self.model, input_type="search_document")
        return response.embeddings

Constructor keyword arguments become the component's params. ragpick validates them against the signature, so a typo in rag.yaml fails with the list of accepted params.

docs.title: In your own code (no packaging needed)
docs.text:
from ragpick import register


@register("embedder", "cohere")
class CohereEmbedder: ...

Import the module before building the pipeline.

docs.title: As an installable package (entry points)
docs.text:
# pyproject.toml of your plugin package
[project.entry-points."ragpick.components"]
"embedder.cohere" = "ragpick_cohere:CohereEmbedder"

The entry-point name is <kind>.<name>. Once the package is installed, type: cohere just works. An entry point whose name has no dot is simply imported, so a module can register several components with @register. Plugins can't shadow built-in names, and a broken plugin is logged and skipped.

docs.title: 3. Use it
docs.text:
blueprint: hybrid
components:
  embedder: {type: cohere, params: {model: embed-english-v3.0}}

docs.title: Dependency injection
docs.text:
Components that need other components declare them as constructor parameters named embedder, store or keyword_index. The pipeline passes them in:

@register("retriever", "mmr")
class MMRRetriever:
    def __init__(self, embedder, store, k: int = 10, diversity: float = 0.3) -> None: ...

    def retrieve(self, query, k, filters=None): ...

docs.title: Rules for stores and indexes
docs.text:
• Honour filters, including the allowed_groups access-control semantics. Reuse ragpick.filters.matches_filters, or translate filters natively as QdrantStore does.
  • Set supports_filters = True on the class so ragpick recommend doesn't warn users who need access control.
  • add must upsert by chunk id, and delete(doc_ids) must remove every chunk of those documents.

docs.title: Testing your plugin
docs.text:
Use the global registry and clean up afterwards, or build an isolated Registry():

from ragpick import Pipeline, registry


def test_my_embedder(tmp_path):
    registry.add("embedder", "mine", MyEmbedder)
    try:
        p = Pipeline.from_dict(
            {
                "blueprint": "naive",
                "index_dir": str(tmp_path),
                "components": {"embedder": {"type": "mine"}},
            }
        )
        p.ingest("tests/data")
        assert p.query("hello").contexts
    finally:
        registry.remove("embedder", "mine")
